name: Fillmed

lead: Fillmed is the laboratory brand behind a range of hyaluronic acid (HA) injectables, marketed under names such as the NCTF 135HA skin booster, the M-HA line and the Artfiller range. They are given by clinicians to hydrate skin, soften fine lines and, in the filler products, add volume to areas such as lips.

Two 2023 randomized studies of Fillmed-brand products report reductions in fine lines and improvements in hydration and radiance, and the NCTF study also reported better self-esteem scores. A 2026 laboratory study included an Artfiller lip product when testing how fast hyaluronidase dissolves lip fillers.

paras: The products are injected into the skin by trained practitioners, usually as a short series of sessions spaced weeks apart for the skin-booster type, with fine-line and radiance changes assessed after the series. Fillers are often combined with other aesthetic treatments.

HA injectables can cause bruising, swelling and redness, and rarely vascular occlusion, which can be treated with hyaluronidase. In the NCTF study, most adverse events were mild. Treatment should be performed by qualified medical professionals.

chain: Hyaluronic acid injected into the skin
Smoother, more hydrated skin and softer fine lines
angle.text: Skin-booster injections target hydration and fine lines, and filler versions add volume where wanted. Studies report improved wrinkles, radiance and hydration after a course of three sessions.

lead: Fillmed is a French laboratory brand of hyaluronic acid injectables, associated with Filorga. Its range includes skin-booster products such as NCTF 135HA and M-HA 10 and shaping fillers such as Artfiller Lips.[1][2][3]
The skin boosters aim at hydration, radiance and fine lines rather than volume, while the filler products add structure. Both depend on HA's ability to bind water.[2]
Research on the brand includes a randomized multicentre study of NCTF 135HA and a split-face placebo-controlled study of M-HA 10, both published in 2023.[1][2]
infobox: Intradermal or filler injection by clinicians

paras: NCTF 135HA is described as a bio-revitalizing solution with hyaluronic acid intended to offset skin dehydration, fatigue and fine wrinkles.[1] M-HA 10 is a non-cross-linked HA preparation from FILLMED Laboratories.[2] The Artfiller range includes a lip product.[3]

In a randomized, active-controlled study, 146 people received three sessions of NCTF 135HA plus moisturizer or moisturizer alone. At days 75 and 120 the injected group had significantly reduced wrinkles around the eyes, neck and decollete and better radiance, with hydration up one week after the last session and higher self-esteem scores.[1] In a split-face study of 30 people, M-HA 10 was compared with saline on the opposite side; ten days after the last of three sessions, crow's feet depth and other measures improved significantly versus control.[2]

Most adverse events in the NCTF study were mild.[1] A laboratory study of six commercial lip fillers, including Fillmed Artfiller Lips, measured how quickly hyaluronidase degrades each one, relevant to treating accidental intravascular injection that can cause ischemia or necrosis.[3]

Two randomized studies in 2023 evaluated Fillmed-brand HA injections and reported improvement in fine lines, hydration and radiance versus control or saline.[1][2] An in vitro 2026 study examined enzyme degradation of Fillmed Artfiller Lips alongside other lip fillers.[3]

timeline.event: Randomized studies of NCTF 135HA and M-HA 10 are published.[1][2]
